reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: THE ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER FOUND A DIVERGENCE BUG I HAD JUST WRITTEN
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: I implemented hunterTriggerScoreForWave by calling readTestHunterTriggerScore() inside the function. That reads `window`. The ?worker=1 Web Worker has no window, so under the E2E seam the host and the worker would compute different hunter triggers and diverge on a value stateHashFull covers. vitest could never catch it because jsdom gives every suite one shared window. A verifier agent - auditing code I had written minutes earlier while it probed - caught it and quoted the line back to me.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: The probe had correctly written out this exact hazard for the win score, and then did not check whether the SIBLING function had it. I made the same mistake in the same file: I honoured the rule where I was thinking about it and violated it one function later. When a hazard is named for one call site, grep for every other site that could have it BEFORE writing the fix - that is the four-sites habit applied to a hazard rather than to a field.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: A REQUIRED PARAMETER TURNED EVERY UNVISITED CALL SITE INTO A COMPILE ERROR
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: Threading the wave into three HUD format functions, I made the new parameter REQUIRED rather than defaulting it to wave 1. tsc immediately produced 16 errors - all of them in tests, none in production, which was itself the proof that production was fully wired.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: A tolerant default would have been faster and strictly worse: a forgotten call site would have shown a permanently-wave-1 bar with NO runtime symptom, which is exactly the tolerant-default hazard S182 recorded (a new union value lost its wording for every goblin and boss because one consumer had a permissive `default` arm). Prefer the compiler telling you where the work is over a default that hides it.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: TWO ANALYSES DISAGREED ABOUT THE CAUSE AND ONLY THE REAL LOOP SETTLED IT
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: One lane concluded FREE_SPARK_SOFT_CAP was destroying the ramp output from wave 7. Its verifier argued a POOL cap cannot throttle an ARRIVAL rate, and that a starving fleet keeps the pool near zero so the cap never fires. Both were plausible on paper and the difference decided what to build. I wrote a fixture that drives stepPhysics through a whole BUILD and FIGHT: peak pool at wave 6-7 was 18-19 against a cap of 24. The cap was NOT binding; the owner hypothesis was right.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: The same fixture then found something neither analysis had: the quarry is EMPTY at every BUILD whistle from wave 2 on, because the reap is unconditional while the spawn dispatch is BUILD-gated. That is the owner "waiting in line" verbatim, and no faucet number removes it. Measuring did not just arbitrate the argument - it produced the finding neither side was looking for. This is the castleGuns.test.ts pattern and it keeps paying.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: AN EARLIER PROPOSAL WAS A NO-OP THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED GREEN
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: A proposed SPAWN_RATE_BANDS formula reduced algebraically to 0.2w + 0.8 - identical to the existing constant at every wave. Its verifier evaluated it and caught that, and also caught that EVERY test the proposal offered to protect the change (band-boundary assertions, monotonicity) passes on a no-op ramp.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: That is the dangerous half: not a wrong formula, but a wrong formula whose own guards cannot see it. I mutation-tested my replacement by neutralising the band factor to 1 - literally that no-op - and required guards to go RED. Four did, including the MEASURED one that drives the real loop and therefore cannot be fooled by source text. Design the guard to fail against the plausible wrong implementation, not against an absurd one.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: THE RIGHT MECHANISM MADE A WHOLE CLASS OF FOLLOW-UP BUG IMPOSSIBLE
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: The stuck carry needed the host to clear state the host cannot see (the local ControlState). A verifier killed the obvious fix: a host-side DROP leaves the spark Free, the client recomputes `mine` as true and keeps lerping it to the cursor, and enforceSpawnerBounds rim-snaps it away. But the owner ruling was the BANK, and banking DELETES the spark from world.freeSparks - the very map `mine` is computed from. The stale gesture then falls through the `!mine` branch that already existed.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: Following the owner ruling exactly produced a fix that needed no client-side companion, where the engineer-obvious variant would have needed one and shipped a second bug. When a ruling looks like a constraint, check whether it is actually the simpler mechanism before treating it as a cost.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: THE CHANGE DID NOT CAUSE THE RED - IT EXPOSED A TEST THAT HAD NEVER WORKED
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: EDGE_PAD 8 -> 0 turned nine of nineteen recipes red in blueprintLegality.test.ts. The probe used blueprintRadius (the CIRCUMRADIUS) while the rule it probes uses blueprintExtent().minDx. At pad 8 the probe happened to land outside the legal area anyway, so the mismatch never showed.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: The instinct under a red suite is to assume the change broke something. Here the change was correct and the TEST had been wrong since it was written - it was only ever passing by coincidence. Read what the test actually asserts before adjusting either side, and re-derive the probe from the same function the rule uses so the two cannot drift again.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: THE HONEST ANSWER WAS THAT GEOMETRY WAS NOT THE BLOCKER
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: The owner reported he cannot build in the bottom band, and the carried research framed it as an off-screen-rule problem needing a canvas-edge ruling. Measuring showed the rule is SYMMETRICAL - the same band is dead at the top and both sides - and that the footer occupies the bottom 84px with guards that swallow clicks ON PURPOSE, because planting under an invisible plate was reported three separate times.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: I shipped the 8px that were genuinely free and did NOT lower the rule further, because that would put towers under a plate whose guards refuse them anyway. The deliverable for a blocked item is a SMALLER, more accurate question than the one inherited: not "may a tower overhang the edge?" but "do you want the footer moved?". Also worth carrying: a loose SHAPE has no edge rule at all, so if he was dropping shapes rather than stamping a tower, the blocker was never this rule.

reflexion_entries_to_archive.headline: THE CLAIM VERIFIER CAUGHT THREE FALSE CLAIMS OF MINE IN ONE RUN
reflexion_entries_to_archive.what_happened: Authoring 42 verification bindings, I claimed ui.ts no longer contains PHASE_1_WIN_SCORE (two stale comments survived, and both were factually wrong as well), wrote one binding whose needle contained placeholder characters so it PASSED vacuously, and wrote a file_lacks broad enough to match a sibling function legitimate throw.
reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: Authoring bindings is not verifying. RUNNING them is. Two of the three would have gone unnoticed forever - one was a green assertion that could never fail. A binding that cannot fail is worse than no binding, because it reads as coverage. Every binding gets executed, and any that passes on the first try against a claim I have not personally grepped gets re-read.
